## Summary
Official Portfolio123 account publishing a **fully-specified five-ETF rotation system** (tweet text truncated mid-sentence — full rules completed below from the sibling run's summary; ranking metric per attached stats card):

- **Universe:** SPY, QQQ, IEF, BND, GLD (US equities large/growth, Treasuries mid/agg, gold — the classic five).
- **Eligibility (trend filter):** an ETF is eligible only if **at least 2 of 3** are true: 6-month total return > 0, 1-year total return > 0, 2-year total return > 0.
- **Ranking:** eligible ETFs ranked on **trend acceleration** (tweet text truncates exactly at the ranking line; full ranking formula + rebalance rules are on the linked Portfolio123 screen page behind the t.co shortlink — not yet opened).
- **Portfolio construction:** hold **top 3 equal weight**, **50% max per ETF**, **weekly rebalance**, unused weight in cash. (From the sibling run's 19:44Z summary of the same tweet.)
- **Backtest stats (from OCR, P123 screen vs SPY/BND 60/40 benchmark):** total return **1,209.85% vs 574.05%**, annualized **9.74% vs 7.14%**, max drawdown **−19.51% vs −34.70%**, monthly Sharpe **0.87 vs 0.55**, Sortino **1.18 vs 0.74**, StdDev **8.78% vs 9.40%** (monthly-period stats per the card), alpha **5.20%**, beta **0.49**, correlation to benchmark **0.53**, R² 0.28. Backtest window 1998–2026(7); the card also plots positions count and turnover %.

## Why it matters
- **First fully-disclosed ETF-rotation node in the vault** — pairs with the same-day [[2026-09-09-l1vsun-yield-curve-aware-momentum]] capture as the two poles of the evidence spectrum: this one is a named vendor (Portfolio123) with a public screen, full rules visible, stats card attached; the L1vsun card is an anonymous AI-generated summary. Useful calibration pair for judging source quality.
- **Mechanically sound design:** the 2-of-3 multi-horizon trend filter is a robustness trick (avoids single-window whipsaw), and capping at 50% per ETF + weekly rebalance + cash fallback controls concentration and over-trading. Same family as the GEM/Keller \& Keuning-style defensive TAA literature and Quantpedia's asset-class momentum rotational system.
- **Backtest realism gates:** stats are from the vendor's own platform (P123 screens are reproducible there, which is a plus), but (1) the ranking metric is behind a truncated link — need the screen page for full replication; (2) 1998–2026 window includes two full bear regimes (good) but 5-ETF universes with gold/agg bonds have strong look-ahead-ish universe selection (all five ETFs existed by 1998 — actually SPY 1993, QQQ 1999 → **QQQ inception 1999 introduces a mild universe inconsistency**, need to check how P123 handled pre-1999 data), (3) monthly Sharpe 0.87 on a ~28-year window is solid-but-not-spectacular — credible, unlike the L1vsun card's 1.87; (4) QQQ inception was 1999 — check how the P123 screen handled the pre-1999 window before treating 1998 as clean.
- **Actionable:** add to the study queue as a candidate simple-TAA baseline to replicate on P123 or in Python; compare against 60/40 and the Milk Man rules on the same window.
